_readme: Camera calibrations. ground.image: near-left, near-right, far-right, far-left corners of a rectangle on the road, picked at frame_size. width_m/length_m: that rectangle in metres; scale_verified=false means nobody measured it, so absolute metres and speeds are nominal (they cancel out of a wait only when the booth is in view). Lanes: across/along are fractions of the rectangle; along may run past [0,1]. booth_distance_m: metres from the strip's booth-end row to the inspection booth, null = not measured (no wait is produced, only queue and speed). cbp_lane: null until someone confirms which CBP lane type the strip is. mask: x,y,w,h overlays (clock, logos, QR codes, signs that hide the road). Check any change with `camera snapshot`. clock: the burned-in date/time box; a stream whose clock stops changing for 20 s is reported frozen. booth_distance_uncertainty_m / booth_distance_verified: a distance estimated from a map carries its +/- and verified=false; the wait's range widens by it and the viewer marks the minutes approximate.

pdn-north.title: Paso del Norte (Norte)
pdn-north.notes: Looks north up the bridge from the Juarez end; the US booths are past the far end, out of view. Cars drive away from the camera, northbound: the owner confirmed the direction on 2026-10-27, so direction_verified is true. The road here has 4 car lanes (owner, 2026-10-27): 3 normal lanes on the left road, each with its own painted arrow, and 1 SENTRI lane on the very right. lane-1..lane-3 (left to right) are the 3 normal lanes; their strips and zones split the carriageway between the yellow left curb and the white bollard line into equal thirds (width assumed 3 x 3.5 m), not traced from the paint. They are read separately because they queue separately: at 03:16 local on 2026-10-19 only the middle lane was queued. The Feliz Viaje sign hides the road behind it and is masked. lane-4 runs between the white bollards and the orange barrels, lane-5 between the barrels and the right curb; their edges were mapped through this rectangle's homography on a daylight frame (bollards at 1.00 of the width at every depth, curb 1.79-1.89, barrels tapering 1.45 to 1.25 where they end). Both are the one SENTRI lane, split in two by the barrels near the camera (owner, 2026-10-27). They stay two strips and two count zones: one zone over both would be ~9 m wide (nominal), and the loop reads two cars abreast in one zone as one car (loop.py), so a car each side of the barrels would be counted once; and one zone would be a new quad, which voids the saved loop roads. At 08:40 local on 2026-10-19 the queue had moved from lanes 1-3 to these two. Booth distance (2026-10-22, Google satellite, map scale bar): from the Feliz Viaje gantry at about 31.7463,-106.4866 north along the bridge to the CBP primary-booth canopy at about 31.7500,-106.4868: ~410 m, +/-30 m. The strips do not end at the gantry: they run on under and past the sign. In a 2026-10-22 snapshot the gantry posts reach the road at about image y 405-420, which this calibration puts ~45 m (nominal; the scale is unverified) short of the strips' booth-end row, so booth_distance_m from that row is 410 - 45 = ~365 m, +/-35 m (map, post feet and scale). The gantry was placed from the layout (the parking lot west of the bridge appears beside the middle of the lanes); Street View has no imagery on the bridge deck to confirm it. Count line A (count_zones) is 1.5 m long and has only ~9.3 m of road in view below its near edge (nominal metres, through this homography), which breaks detect.py's zone rule (a car seen whole in 3 frames before the zone) above ~6 m/s. So line A undercounts free flow, and a transit reads that as drift: on rendered scenes (2026-10-26 audit) the loop counter missed ~30 % of cars at 5-6 m/s with random gaps, the YOLOX counter ~9 % at 8 m/s. ASSUMPTION: free-flow speeds at line A are unmeasured. Owner task, from a daylight frame: redraw line A ~3 m long with ~18 m of road in view below its near edge, and delete pdn-north.loop.npz so a stale road is not seeded. Lane types (owner, QUESTIONS.md Q-22): on 2026-10-26 lane-5 was named SENTRI and lanes 1-4 normal; on 2026-10-27 the owner said lane-4 and lane-5 are both the SENTRI lane, so both their count zones are typed sentri. lane-1..lane-3 are normal: standard and Ready, not told apart (ASSUMPTION), so their zones are typed normal. Line A thus has 3 normal zones and 2 sentri zones. The lane type lives on the count zones, which the runner and combine measure by. Every strip keeps cbp_lane null, lane-4 and lane-5 included: a strip's number is the queue reader's (D+L)/v with the booths ~365 m out of view, which ADR-0015 rejects as a wait and which under-reads at lane-5, so it must not be labelled SENTRI on the card or filed as a car_sentri signal until it is checked against timed crossings. Typing the zones, retyping lane-4 and confirming the direction moved no zone or strip, so the saved loop roads still hold.

lerdo-north.title: Lerdo (Norte)
lerdo-north.notes: Looks north along the Lerdo-Stanton bridge from the Juarez end. right-roadway is the straight stretch between the bollard line and the orange right curb, with the northbound arrow; width assumed two lanes (7 m). CBP names this port 'Stanton DCL', but which lane type the strip is has not been confirmed. Below y=380 the roadway curves left toward the camera and is not covered by the straight strip. Booth distance (2026-10-22, Google satellite): from the overpass over Av. Heroico Colegio Militar, visible at the top of this camera's picture, at about 31.7474,-106.4824, along the bridge to the Stanton commuter-lane booth canopy at about 31.7502,-106.4833; ~335 m, +/-35 m. Not yet corrected to the strip's booth-end row: that row sits short of the far gantry at the top of the picture by a gap this calibration cannot measure (the road climbs there, so the flat-road warp does not hold past the strip), so 335 m is likely an under-estimate.

pdn-south-street.title: Paso del Norte (Sur)
pdn-south-street.notes: Looks south down the Juarez street that feeds the Paso del Norte bridge; the queue faces the camera and drives toward it, so the booth end is the near end and the bridge is behind the camera. No lane markings (cobblestone); the two strips follow the two queue columns seen at 04:56 local on 2026-10-19, left along the barrier fence. Vendors walk between the columns. Width assumed ~9 m. Booth distance (2026-10-22, Google satellite): the camera is placed at the north end of this street near the foot of the bridge (~31.7457,-106.4865), not confirmed; from there up Av. Benito Juarez and across the bridge to the CBP primary booths at about 31.7500,-106.4868: ~480 m, +/-70 m. That is from the camera; the strips' booth-end row is in front of it, ~30 m (nominal) by the camera position this calibration implies (height ~14 m; square pixels and a centred image assumed), so booth_distance_m is ~510 m, +/-75 m.

bota-south-approach.title: Córdova - Américas (Sur)
bota-south-approach.notes: Looks south down the approach road to the Bridge of the Americas, with the bridge behind the camera. The queue in the left carriageway drives toward the camera: the reader's signed speed was negative in all 15 rounds from 03:16 to 07:56 local on 2026-10-19 with the booth set at the far end, so it is set at the near end. (Red lights seen on these cars at night had suggested the opposite; the measurement overruled that.) Two lanes, width assumed 7 m. The right carriageway carries other traffic and is not calibrated. BOTA is not administered by FPFCH (on-screen banner). Booth distance (2026-10-22, Google satellite): the camera is placed on Av. de las Americas south of the Mexican plaza (~31.7616,-106.4519) from the flag monument and visitor-centre sign on its right, not confirmed; from there north across the bridge to the CBP primary booths at about 31.7669,-106.4511: ~600 m, +/-70 m. That is from the camera; the strips' booth-end row is in front of it, ~17 m (nominal) by the camera position this calibration implies (height ~11 m; square pixels and a centred image assumed), so booth_distance_m is ~615 m, +/-70 m.

lerdo-south-booths.title: Lerdo (Sur)
lerdo-south-booths.notes: Lerdo, booths in the foreground: cars drive toward the camera and stop at gates staffed by uniformed officers, so the booth end is the near end and the booth is in view (booth_distance_m 0), which makes this the one calibration whose wait does not depend on its unverified scale. Direction is INFERRED as southbound (Mexican customs on arrival in Juarez) from the officers and the flow toward the Juarez end; not confirmed, hence direction_verified false. Two lanes split at the orange divider; width assumed 7 m.

city-pdn-north.title: City of El Paso bridge camera: Paso del Norte (bridgepdn1)
city-pdn-north.notes: The US half of the Paso del Norte bridge, from the City of El Paso's Bridge Cameras page (https://www2.elpasotexas.gov/misc/externally_linked/bridges/cameras.html), read at the owner's risk and NEVER displayed on our pages (ADR-0014, QUESTIONS.md Q-21). A wide-angle camera low at the left (west) wall, looking north-east across the northbound lanes toward the CBP canopy at the top left of the picture; well lit at night (checked 19:59 local, 2026-10-24). No burned-in clock: frames are timed by segment Last-Modified (hls.py). Line B (count_zones) was redrawn on 2026-10-26 from two daylight frames of that afternoon (16:28 and 16:48 local), used for the redraw only with the owner's leave; Q-21 stands, and no City picture is shown or kept. In both frames the cars are seen from behind, nose toward the canopy, queued in columns toward it, so direction_verified is true. Columns per Q-22: col-1..col-4 are the car columns left of the white posts, numbered from the left wall (lane_type normal: standard and Ready, not told apart, ASSUMPTION); col-e is column E, right of the white posts, between them and the right railing (lane_type sentri). The band along the left wall has no zone: it was empty in both frames while every other column was queued, has cones at its far end, and is about 1-2 m wide by the model below, too narrow for a car; col-1 starts at its edge line. If a car is ever seen in it, give it a zone. How they were drawn: a rough model of the camera from the 16:48 frame (lens distortion from the straightened left railing, a lane line and the post line; focal length and tilt from the posts and fence pillars; scale from three cars' wheelbases, which put the camera about 3-4 m up: ASSUMPTION, nothing was measured on site), each zone 3.5 m long across its column at about 10-13.5 m north of the camera. col-e was drawn by hand on the foot of the posts and of the railing, where the model is least sure; no car was in column E in either frame, so its place is not yet confirmed by a car. About 5-9 m of road (col-e least) is in view before each zone, short of detect.py's 18 m rule, so the counts hold at queue speeds only, up to about 3 m/s at col-e and 6 m/s at col-2 (ASSUMPTION: cars this close to the booths mostly queue). Higher up, the lanes are seen so edge-on that a zone's edges nearly run along the traffic, and column E vanishes behind the cars of col-4. Seen this low and from the side, a car's body covers, in the picture, the zone of the column beyond it (col-4 cars cover col-e, col-1 cars col-2): the yolox counter counts by a box's foot, but the loop counter does count such a car again in the next column. In both daylight frames a col-4 car covers col-e, and in a rendered pass (synthetic frames) the loop counted such cars at col-e: 3 times each with lengths read from square pixels, and still 2 for 6 cars with the zones' "metres" given below (line-B review, 2026-10-26; re-run 2026-10-27). So col-e is counted by yolox only ("methods"), and the runner does not measure the loop's SENTRI; lift that only after a 15-min hand count at col-e. Each zone carries "metres": [3.5, 3.5]: the width is loop.ASSUMED_LANE_M (ASSUMPTION) and the length is the 3.5 m the rough model drew (ASSUMPTION). Without them loop.py read col-1 as about 1.4 m long and col-e as about 6.7 m, so its thresholds in metres were off by those ratios, and no two columns matched in length, which turned off its judging of a car across a column line (loop._beside). Now col-1..col-4 are judged in pairs, as line A's lanes are. This does not take back a car whose body covers the next column in the picture: that body is wider than CAR_MAX_M. So the loop's normal count at B also counts col-1..col-3 cars again in col-2..col-4 (by how much is not measured; ASSUMPTION), and the runner still measures it: the anchors' drift line takes up part of it, and it cannot vote until a 15-min hand count of the normal columns, taken with col-1 queued, puts it within 5 % (Q-24). If that hand count fails, give col-2..col-4 "methods": ["yolox"] too, which leaves the loop's normal not measured. The new patch shapes make seed() refuse the saved City roads, so the loop relearns them. None of this is verified by a hand count yet. The camera shows faces through windscreens and plates at close range: frames are only processed in memory and nothing is cropped, read or stored.
